classification.difficultyReason: Interpret horizontal substitutions and rearrange y−1=h(x) or y−1=g(x), then translate the supplied turning points, joins and whole graph shapes on common axes. Each part applies one taught translation directly; unfamiliar shapes require preserving features but no new function rule or combined transformation.

content.prompt: In each case an unknown function has been drawn. Draw the functions specified below each graph on the same axes.

spec.description: Unknown smooth curve reconstructed with Bézier segments through its supplied intercepts and turning points. Axes extend to accommodate the requested drawings.
spec.mathematics: Zeros −2, 0, 2; local maximum (−1,1); local minimum (1,−1). No equation is asserted.

answer.worked: Move every point 2 units right. The turning points become $(1,1)$ and $(3,-1)$, and the zeros become $0$, $2$ and $4$.
Move every point 1 unit left. The turning points become $(-2,1)$ and $(0,-1)$, and the zeros become $-3$, $-1$ and $1$.

spec.description: Unknown smooth graph with two minima and a central maximum, reconstructed from the supplied coordinate cues. Extra horizontal axis length accommodates the requested left translations.
spec.mathematics: Minimum (−2,0), point (−1,1), maximum (0,2), minimum (1,1), point (2,2). No global polynomial is asserted.

answer.worked: Subtract 2 from every $x$-coordinate. The minima become $(-4,0)$ and $(-1,1)$, and the maximum becomes $(-2,2)$. The points $(-1,1)$ and $(2,2)$ move to $(-3,1)$ and $(0,2)$.
Subtract 1 from every $x$-coordinate. The minima become $(-3,0)$ and $(0,1)$, and the maximum becomes $(-1,2)$. The points $(-1,1)$ and $(2,2)$ move to $(-2,1)$ and $(1,2)$.

spec.description: Straight left ray meeting a curved right branch at the corner (0,1), with minimum (1,0), guide through (2,1), and the supplied negative y tick.
spec.mathematics: Left branch through (−1,0) and (0,1); curved branch through (0,1), (1,0), (2,1). The quadratic representation reproduces the supplied branch shape.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y-1&=h(x)\\y&=h(x)+1.\end{align*}$$
Add 1 to every $y$-coordinate. The join becomes $(0,2)$ and the minimum becomes $(1,1)$. The marked points become $(-1,1)$ and $(2,2)$.
Subtract 1 from every $y$-coordinate. The join becomes $(0,0)$ and the minimum becomes $(1,-1)$. The marked points become $(-1,-1)$ and $(2,0)$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y-1&=g(x)\\y&=g(x)+1.\end{align*}$$
The arc endpoints become $(-1,1)$ and $(1,1)$, and its highest point becomes $(0,2)$. Move both outer rays up 1 unit with the arc.
The arc endpoints become $(0,0)$ and $(2,0)$, and its highest point becomes $(1,1)$. Move both outer rays right 1 unit with the arc.
